reason: This Hebrew biblical text (Exodus 1:1-7) presents a fundamentally different leadership model. Moses and Aaron, the righteous leaders, are characterized by obedience to God's commands, compassionate mediation on behalf of the oppressed Israelites, and proclamation of God's liberating message—not by violence toward any people. When the Israelites themselves struggle to listen due to their suffering ('shortness of spirit'), the response is continued divine assistance, not correction through violence. God's judgment against obstinate Pharaoh comes through divine plagues, which are presented as God's direct miraculous action, not as a human leadership model to emulate. The entire narrative arc emphasizes liberation of the oppressed and faithful, non-violent mediation as the hallmarks of good leadership.
